questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

Each and every individual has the ________ to follow her/his own religion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Freedom**.

__
 
• The sentence talks about the right of an individual to choose their own religion.
 
• '**Freedom**' is the most appropriate word to fill in the blank, as it signifies the right to make a choice without any compulsion or restriction.
 
• Grammatically, '**freedom**' is a noun and fits well in the sentence structure.
 
• Other options like 'compulsion', 'economy', and 'expulsion' do not convey the intended meaning of the sentence.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.

**Complete sentence**: *Each and every individual has the freedom __to follow her/his own religion.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Compulsion **means forcing someone to do something.
 
• **Economy **refers to the system of production, distribution, and consumption of goods and services.
 
• **Expulsion **means removing someone from a place or organization.

questions.question:
**Select the correct spelling of the underlined word in the following sentence.**

The cowboys were injured badly as they were involved in a __dual__.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**duel**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The correct spelling of the underlined word in the sentence is "**duel**," not "dual."
 
• The word "**duel**" means a formal fight between two people.
 
• It is spelt with a "**u**" after the "**d**", not two "l's".
 
• "**Dual**" is an adjective that means having two parts or components. It describes something that is double or twofold in nature.
 
• "**Duel**" is a noun that refers to a formal combat or fight between two individuals or groups, typically with weapons. It's often used to settle a dispute or defend honour.
 
• 
 
In the sentence, the context suggests that the cowboys were injured because they were involved in a fight or combat situation, not because they were associated with something double or having two parts.

 
 
• 
 
Therefore, the correct word is "**duel**," which denotes a fight, making the sentence mean that the cowboys were injured badly because they were engaged in a duel.

 

Therefore, **option 2** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.**

Rain on someone’s parade

options.text: To spoil and ruin a happy moment
To restore the disturbed law and order situation
To blame and hurt an innocent child
To test and check a brilliant student

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To spoil and ruin a happy moment.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The idiom "**rain on someone's parade**" means to spoil or ruin a happy moment or celebration.

 
 
• **Example**: "*Sarah was excited about her promotion at work, but her colleague Mark rained on her parade by pointing out all the extra responsibilities she would now have to handle.*"
 
 
 
• It is often used to describe someone who brings bad news or negativity to a situation that was previously joyful.
 
• The phrase can be used in both literal and figurative senses, such as rain literally ruining an outdoor event or someone's negative attitude ruining the mood.
 
• The idiom is informal and commonly used in spoken English.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 1**

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.**

What __is the qualities__ of a good teacher?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**are the qualities**".

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence "What is the qualities of a good teacher?" contains an error. 
 
• The error is in subject-verb agreement. The word "**qualities**" is a plural noun, and the verb that follows should also be in the plural form, which is "**are**."
 
• In the original sentence, the singular verb "**is**" is used, which does not agree in number with the plural noun "qualities."
 
• **Subject-verb agreement** is a grammatical rule that dictates that the verb in a sentence must agree in number with its subject.
 
• In this case, when the subject is plural, as in "qualities," the verb should also be in the plural form, such as "are."
 
• **Corrected Sentence**: *What are the qualities of a good teacher?*
 
• In this corrected sentence, "**are**" matches the plural noun "**qualities**," resulting in correct subject-verb agreement.

Therefore, **option 3** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
**Select the correct word for the blanks in the given sentence.**

My sister ________ lift a box of 5 kilograms and I have a ________ of carrot juice.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Can**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• In the first part of the sentence, "**can**" is used as a **modal verb** to express the ability or capability to do something.
 
• When used in this way, "**can**" indicates that someone has the physical or skill-related capacity to perform an action.
 
 
• **For example**, "My sister can lift a box of 5 kilograms" means that she has the strength or skill to do so.
 
 
 
• In the second part of the sentence, "**can**" is used as a **noun **to refer to a container or tin of carrot juice.
 
• When talking about food or beverages, the word "**can**" is commonly used to describe the packaging or container.
 
• This usage is common when referring to food or drink containers.
 
 
• **For instance**, you might say, "I have a can of soda" to refer to a soda container.
 
 
 
• So, "**can**" is the correct word for both blanks because it serves as a modal verb to indicate ability in the first blank and as a noun to describe a container in the second blank.

Hence, **option 2** is the correct answer.

**Complete sentence**: *My sister can __lift a box of 5 kilograms and I have a __can __of carrot juice.*

questions.question:

• When we use "will" to express a future action, we typically follow it with the base form of the verb (infinitive form).
 
• In this case, the correct form of the verb to use after "will" is "**drive**," which is the base form (**infinitive**) of the verb.
 
• **The correct sentence would be** *"I will drive you to the station in the morning."*
 
• In this corrected sentence, we have the future tense "**will drive**," which is the grammatically accurate way to express that you will be the one driving to the station in the morning.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 2**.
